intro.en: Effectual comes from Latin efficere, to work out, through the participle effectus, a thing worked out; the suffix -ual says able to produce that result.
intro.cn: effectual 来自拉丁语 efficere（做出、促成），经由分词 effectus（做出来的东西，即结果）；后缀 -ual 表示「能产生那个结果的」。

items.en: Latin efficere means to work out or bring about, from ex- plus facere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 efficere 意为做出、促成，由 ex- 加 facere 构成。

items.en: The participle effectus names a thing worked out, a result.
items.cn: 分词 effectus 指做出来的东西，即结果。

items.en: Medieval Latin added -alis to build effectualis, able to produce a result.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语加 -alis 构成 effectualis，意为能产生结果的。

items.en: English took effectual in the 14C for a prayer or remedy that truly worked.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借用 effectual，指真正起作用的祷告或药方。

items.en: Lawyers used effectual for a deed or statute that carried binding force.
items.cn: 律师用 effectual 指有约束力的契据或法令。

items.en: Effective became the everyday word and effectual kept a formal, older tone.
items.cn: effective 成为日常用词，effectual 保留了较正式、较古旧的语气。

note.en: Effectual, effective and effectuate all grow from Latin facere, to make; the endings tell you whether the word names a quality, an adverb or an action.
note.cn: effectual、effective 与 effectuate 都源于拉丁语 facere（做）；词尾告诉你它指的是性质、方式还是动作。

dict_mnemonic.text: effectual ＝ ef-（向外，ex- 的变体）＋ fect（做，拉丁 facere）＋ -ual（形容词后缀，能…的）＝「能做出结果的」。同一条拉丁词根按词尾分家：-us → effect 结果；-ive → effective 有效的（日常首选）；-ual → effectual 奏效的（偏正式、偏古旧，也用于法律「有效的」）；-ually → effectually 奏效地；-uate → effectuate 使生效。想说「这药有效」日常用 effective 或 works，effectual 多出现在旧文献、法律文本与宗教写作里。注意与 efficient（有效率的，强调少浪费）区分：effectual 只看结果有没有出来，efficient 还看花了多少力气。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ facere（做）→ efficere（促成）→ effectus（结果）→ effectual（奏效的）

scene: 工厂换掉漏气的管道后，每吨产品的耗电降了一半。Engineers measured the gain in efficiency at every stage.

senses.title: Output compared with input
senses.definition: the ratio of useful work or output to the energy, time or effort supplied

senses.example: The new engine raises fuel efficiency by a fifth.
senses.exampleCN: 新发动机把燃油效率提高了五分之一。
senses.why: Efficientia named the power of a cause to produce an effect; measured, that power becomes a ratio of output to input.
senses.whyCN: efficientia 指原因产生效果的力量；一旦被测量，这份力量就成为产出与投入之比。

senses.title: Working well without waste
senses.definition: the quality of doing something well with little waste of time, money or energy
senses.definitionCN: 把事情做好而很少浪费时间、金钱或精力的品质
senses.example: The office is known for its efficiency.
senses.exampleCN: 这个办公室以高效著称。
senses.why: A thing that produces its effect without waste is efficient, and the quality it shows is efficiency.
senses.whyCN: 不浪费却能产生效果的东西是 efficient，而它显露出的这种品质就是 efficiency。

senses.title: A measured instance of such a ratio
senses.definition: a particular measurement or instance of efficient performance, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某一具体的效率测量结果或表现，常用复数
senses.example: The report compares the efficiencies of three plants.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了三家工厂的效率值。
senses.why: Once the ratio is counted, each count becomes a noun of its own, so the plural names separate figures.
senses.whyCN: 比值一旦被计数，每个计数就各自成为一个名词，于是复数指一项项分开的数字。

items.en: Engineering and economics turned the abstract power into a measured ratio.
items.cn: 工程学与经济学把这种抽象力量变成可测量的比值。

normal.en: The same tank of fuel, a longer drive: that is fuel efficiency.
normal.cn: 同一桶油跑得更远，这就是 fuel efficiency。

normal.en: An office with efficiency gets the work done and leaves the lights off.
normal.cn: 高效的办公室把活干完，还顺手把灯关掉。

normal.en: Efficiency is the ratio; efficiencies are the separate figures you compare.
normal.cn: efficiency 是比值；efficiencies 是你拿来比较的一项项数字。

normal.en: Efficient is the adjective, efficiency the quality it shows.
normal.cn: efficient 是形容词，efficiency 是它显露出的品质。

abstract.en: Picture one barrel of oil and two cars leaving the same line.
abstract.cn: 想象一桶油和两辆从同一条线出发的车。

abstract.en: The farther car turns the same barrel into more distance.
abstract.cn: 跑得更远的那辆车把同一桶油变成了更多里程。

abstract.en: Efficiency is that comparison written as a number.
abstract.cn: efficiency 就是把这种比较写成一个数字。

examples.en: The new engine raises fuel efficiency by a fifth.
examples.cn: 新发动机把燃油效率提高了五分之一。

examples.en: The office is known for its efficiency.
examples.cn: 这个办公室以高效著称。

examples.en: The report compares the efficiencies of three plants.
examples.cn: 报告比较了三家工厂的效率值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊菲申西」——漏气管道一换，同样的电做出更多产品

root: 拉丁语 facere「做」加 ex-「出」构成 efficere「完成」，其名词 efficientia 指「产生效果的力量」，经法语 efficience 进入英语，后转为可测量的产出投入之比。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of efficiency: the ratio of output to input, the quality of working without waste, and a measured instance of that ratio.
sensesIntro.cn: efficiency 的三个义项：产出与投入之比、不浪费地做好事情的品质，以及一项具体的效率测量值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one barrel of fuel carried farther by the better car.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一桶油，被更好的那辆车跑得更远。

branches.en: THE RATIO: useful output divided by what was put in.
branches.cn: 比值线：有用产出除以投入。

branches.en: THE HABIT: the work is done well and little is thrown away.
branches.cn: 习惯线：活干得好，扔掉的少。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: each measurement stands as its own count.
branches.cn: 数字线：每一次测量各自成为一项数字。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: a ratio only means something when figures are set side by side.
branches.cn: 比较线：比值只有把数字并排放在一起才有意义。

branches.en: THE SAVING: less waste is exactly what lifts the ratio.
branches.cn: 节约线：少浪费正是把比值抬上去的东西。

intro.en: Efficiency is a Latin-derived noun in -ency; English builds the adjective efficient and its adverb on the same stem.
intro.cn: efficiency 是以 -ency 收尾的拉丁语来源名词；英语在同一词干上构成形容词 efficient 及其副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin efficere and efficientia are recorded, so only the Indo-European base of facere is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 efficere 与 efficientia 均有记录，只有 facere 的印欧词基属于重构。

definition_zh: 高效的；能干的；有产生力的
definition_en: working well with little waste, organized and capable, or having the power to produce an effect
core_image: 一条流水线，零件进来，成品出去，地上没有剩料
scene: 换上新电机后，同样的活只用一半时间就干完了。The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
sceneCN: 这里 efficient 是「高效的」（第 1 个义项：以较少的投入完成同样的工作）；句意是新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。

pos.zh: 高效的；能干的；有产生力的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

senses.title: Working without waste
senses.definition: working well and completely, with little waste of time, energy or materials
senses.definitionCN: 做事又好又完整，很少浪费时间、精力或材料
senses.example: The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。
senses.why: Efficient is the Latin efficiens, doing or accomplishing: a thing that gets the work done without spending more than it must.
senses.whyCN: efficient 是拉丁语 efficiens，意为「正在做成的」：把活干成，却不比必须的多花一分。

senses.title: Organized and capable
senses.definition: of a person, organized and able to do a job well and quickly
senses.definitionCN: 指人时，有条理、能把事情做好做快
senses.example: She is an efficient manager who never wastes a meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个能干的经理，从不开没有结果的会。
senses.why: A person who finishes work without waste shows the same power to accomplish, so the adjective moves from machines to people.
senses.whyCN: 不浪费却把活完成的人，显露的是同一种「做成」的力量，于是这个形容词从机器移到了人身上。

senses.title: Having the power to produce an effect
senses.definition: having the power to bring about a result, as in the technical phrase efficient cause
senses.definitionCN: 具有产生结果的力量，用于「动力因」这一术语
senses.example: In philosophy, an efficient cause is what brings something about.
senses.exampleCN: 在哲学里，动力因就是使某物产生的东西。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply producing: an efficient cause is the doer that makes the effect exist.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是「产生」：动力因是让结果存在起来的那个施行者。

intro.en: Efficient comes from Latin efficiens, the present participle of efficere, to accomplish, and reached English through French.
intro.cn: efficient 来自拉丁语 efficiens，即 efficere（完成）的现在分词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make and supplied the base of the verb.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」，提供这个动词的词基。

items.en: Ex- out plus facere formed efficere, to work out or accomplish.
items.cn: 表示「出」的 ex- 加 facere 构成 efficere，意为「做出、完成」。

items.en: The participle efficiens described something as accomplishing or producing.
items.cn: 分词 efficiens 描述某物正在完成或正在产生。

items.en: French passed the adjective on with the sense of producing a result.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词传下来，意思是「能产生结果的」。

items.en: Industry added the everyday sense of working without waste of time or fuel.
items.cn: 工业又加入了日常义：不浪费时间或燃料地把活干好。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the efficiency family; the near-meaning group separates effective, productive and economical.
note.cn: 形近组收 efficiency 词族；近义组区分 effective、productive 与 economical。

entries.definition: The quality of working without waste, or the output-to-input ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「效率」，即不浪费的品质或产出投入之比。

entries.definition: In a manner that wastes little time or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「高效地」，很少浪费时间或精力。

entries.definition: The power to reach the intended result, with no claim about waste.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「有效性」，只管结果达没达到，不管浪不浪费。

entries.definition: Producing the result wanted; it asks whether the aim is reached, not what it cost.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有效的」，只问目标是否达到，不问成本。

entries.definition: Producing a good amount of work or goods; it stresses output.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多产的」，强调产出量。

entries.definition: Saving money or resources; it stresses the cost spared.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「节约的」，强调省下的花费。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line that leaves no scrap on the floor, then move to a tidy manager and to a cause that makes things happen.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一条地上没有剩料的流水线出发，再走到干练的经理与「让事情发生」的原因。

normal.en: Efficient means the same work with less fuel, less time and less scrap.
normal.cn: efficient 就是用更少的燃料、时间和废料完成同样的活。

normal.en: An efficient manager ends the meeting when the decision is made.
normal.cn: 能干的经理在决定做出时就结束会议。

normal.en: Efficient and effective are cousins: one saves, the other arrives.
normal.cn: efficient 与 effective 是表亲：一个讲省，一个讲结果到了。

normal.en: The old philosophical sense is plain: efficient cause means the doer.
normal.cn: 古老的哲学义很直白：efficient cause 就是那个施行者。

normal.en: Efficiency is the noun, efficiently the adverb, inefficient the opposite.
normal.cn: efficiency 是名词，efficiently 是副词，inefficient 是反义。

abstract.en: Picture a factory line with parts going in and products coming out.
abstract.cn: 想象一条工厂流水线，零件进去，成品出来。

abstract.en: Look at the floor: nothing usable is left lying there.
abstract.cn: 再看地面：没有还能用的东西被丢在那里。

abstract.en: Efficient is that picture of full output and empty waste.
abstract.cn: efficient 就是「产出满、废料空」的那幅图。

examples.en: The new motor is twice as efficient as the old one.
examples.cn: 新电机比旧电机效率高一倍。

examples.en: She is an efficient manager who never wastes a meeting.
examples.cn: 她是个能干的经理，从不开没有结果的会。

examples.en: In philosophy, an efficient cause is what brings something about.
examples.cn: 在哲学里，动力因就是使某物产生的东西。

root: 拉丁语 facere「做」加 ex-「出」构成 efficere「完成」，其现在分词 efficiens 指「正在做成的」，经法语 efficient 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of efficient: working without waste, a person who is organized and capable, and the technical sense of producing an effect.
sensesIntro.cn: efficient 的三个义项：不浪费地把活干好、人干练有条理，以及「能产生结果」的术语义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a production line with parts going in, products coming out, and no scrap on the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条流水线，零件进去，成品出来，地上没有剩料。

branches.en: THE SAVING: the same work is done with less fuel and less scrap.
branches.cn: 节省线：同样的活，用更少的燃料与废料完成。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a worker whose desk and schedule leave no waste.
branches.cn: 人物线：桌面与日程都不留浪费的工作者。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: the doer that makes the result exist.
branches.cn: 原因线：让结果存在起来的那个施行者。

branches.en: THE POWER: both senses are about producing, one with economy and one in philosophy.
branches.cn: 力量线：两个义项都关乎「产生」，一个讲节省，一个讲哲学。

branches.en: THE HABIT: a person can be as efficient as a well-tuned machine.
branches.cn: 习惯线：人可以像调好的机器一样高效。

intro.en: Efficient carries the Latin participle ending -ens; English adds -ency, -ly and the negative prefix in-.
intro.cn: efficient 带着拉丁语分词词尾 -ens；英语再加 -ency、-ly 与否定前缀 in-。

definition_zh: 努力；费力；尝试；成果；（集体的）行动
definition_en: the use of physical or mental energy, an attempt, a piece of work judged by its quality, or an organized campaign
core_image: 一根绳子被拉到最紧，掌心留下绳纹
scene: 他连着拉了十次绳子，帆才终于升到顶。It took a great effort to raise the sail.
sceneCN: 这里 effort 是「力气、努力」（第 1 个义项：身体或精神上的用力）；句意是升起船帆费了很大力气。

pos.zh: 努力；费力；尝试；成果；集体行动

senses.title: Physical or mental exertion
senses.definition: the use of energy, strength or thought in order to do something
senses.definitionCN: 为了做成某事而付出的精力、力气或心思
senses.example: It took a great effort to raise the sail.
senses.exampleCN: 升起船帆费了很大力气。
senses.why: Effort comes from a French verb meaning to force or strengthen: it is strength put out on purpose.
senses.whyCN: effort 来自一个意为「用力、使强壮」的法语动词：它是有意拿出来的力气。

senses.title: An attempt
senses.definition: an act of trying to do something, especially when success is not certain
senses.definitionCN: 试图做成某事的行动，尤指结果并不确定时
senses.example: He made one last effort to reach the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 他拼尽最后一番努力想游到岸边。
senses.why: A burst of strength aimed at a goal is also a try, so effort names the attempt itself.
senses.whyCN: 朝目标爆发的一股力气也是一次尝试，于是 effort 也指尝试本身。

senses.title: A piece of work judged by its quality
senses.definition: a particular attempt or achievement, often judged as good or poor
senses.definitionCN: 某一次尝试或成果，常被评价为好或差
senses.example: Her first novel was a fine effort.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说是部不错的作品。
senses.why: What has been produced by exerted strength can stand as the work itself, so the effort is the result.
senses.whyCN: 用力之后产出的东西可以当作作品本身，于是这份努力就成了成果。

senses.title: An organized campaign
senses.definition: a coordinated attempt by a group of people, often for aid, rescue or change
senses.definitionCN: 一群人协调一致的行动，常指援助、救援或推动改变
senses.example: The relief effort reached the village by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 救援行动在中午前抵达了村子。
senses.why: Many people putting out strength together form one shared effort, so the word can name a whole campaign.
senses.whyCN: 许多人一起把力气拿出来，汇成一份共同的努力，于是这个词可以指整场行动。

intro.en: Effort comes from Old French esforz, from the verb esforcier, to force or strengthen, and goes back to Latin fortis, strong.
intro.cn: effort 来自古法语 esforz，源自动词 esforcier（用力、使强壮），更早追溯到拉丁语 fortis（强壮的）。

items.en: Fortis meant strong, and it is the root of force and effort alike.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮的」，是 force 与 effort 共同的根。

items.en: Fortia named strength or force, the quality that can be put out.
items.cn: fortia 指力量或强力，即可以被拿出来的那种品质。

items.en: The verb meant to force, strengthen or exert oneself.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「使劲、加强、竭力」。

items.en: The noun named an exertion, a striving or a feat of strength.
items.cn: 名词指一次用力、一番拼搏或一场力量之举。

items.en: English borrowed it for the act of trying hard and later for the attempt itself.
items.cn: 英语借入后表示「努力去做」，后来又指尝试本身。

items.en: The sense of a shared campaign grew from many people exerting themselves together.
items.cn: 「共同行动」一义由许多人一起用力的情形发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on effort; the near-meaning group separates attempt, exertion and endeavor.
note.cn: 形近组收由 effort 构成的词；近义组区分 attempt、exertion 与 endeavor。

entries.definition: Needing no effort; formed from effort with -less.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毫不费力的」，由 effort 加 -less 构成。

entries.definition: In a way that shows no effort; effortless plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「毫不费力地」，由 effortless 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Requiring noticeable effort; effort plus -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「费力的」，由 effort 加 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: An act of trying; it names the try more than the strength spent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「尝试」，更强调「试」而不是花掉多少力气。

entries.definition: Hard physical or mental work; it stresses the strain itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「费力、劳累」，强调承受的紧张。

entries.definition: A serious attempt or undertaking; more formal and more purposeful.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「努力、事业」，更正式、更有目标感。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow one rope pulled tight, then a last try, then a finished piece and a shared rescue.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着一根拉紧的绳子，再走到最后一次尝试、一件成品与一场共同救援。

normal.en: Effort is strength put out on purpose.
normal.cn: effort 就是有意拿出来的力气。

normal.en: The rope leaves its mark on the palm: that mark is effort.
normal.cn: 绳子在掌心留下纹路：那道纹就是 effort。

normal.en: One last pull can be both an effort and an attempt.
normal.cn: 最后一把拉，既是一份力气，也是一次尝试。

normal.en: A fine effort is a piece of work you judge, not a muscle you measure.
normal.cn: a fine effort 是你评价的作品，不是你测量的肌肉。

normal.en: A relief effort is many people's strength gathered into one campaign.
normal.cn: relief effort 是许多人的力气汇成一场行动。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled until it hums.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子被拉到发出嗡响。

abstract.en: The same pull can be a try, a finished work, or a village rescue.
abstract.cn: 同一次拉，可以是一次尝试、一件成品，或一场村庄救援。

abstract.en: Effort is what it costs to move something that does not move by itself.
abstract.cn: effort 就是推动一个自己不会动的东西所要付出的代价。

examples.en: It took a great effort to raise the sail.
examples.cn: 升起船帆费了很大力气。

examples.en: He made one last effort to reach the shore.
examples.cn: 他拼尽最后一番努力想游到岸边。

examples.en: The relief effort reached the village by noon.
examples.cn: 救援行动在中午前抵达了村子。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of effort: exertion, an attempt, a piece of work judged by quality, and an organized campaign.
sensesIntro.cn: effort 的四个义项：用力、尝试、被评价的成果，以及有组织的集体行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope pulled tight, leaving its mark on the palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子被拉到最紧，掌心留下绳纹。

branches.en: THE STRAIN: energy of body or mind put into the work.
branches.cn: 用力线：身体或心思被投进工作里的能量。

branches.en: THE TRY: the same burst of strength aimed at a goal.
branches.cn: 尝试线：同一股力气朝着目标使出去。

branches.en: THE WORK: what the strength produced, judged as good or poor.
branches.cn: 成果线：力气产出的东西，被评好或评差。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: many people's strength gathered into one action.
branches.cn: 行动线：许多人的力气汇成一次行动。

branches.en: ONE PULL: every attempt begins with strength deliberately spent.
branches.cn: 同一把拉：每次尝试都从有意花掉的力气开始。

intro.en: Effort is a French noun in -t built on a verb of forcing; English adds -less, -ful and -ly.

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis and fortia are recorded; the French verb and noun are attested, so no layer here is reconstructed except the oldest root.

items.example: It names strength as a thing.
items.exampleCN: 它把力量作为一个事物来命名。

definition_zh: v. 流出；涌出；散发 adj. （植物、贝壳）平展的；散开的
definition_en: to pour out or flow forth; to give off light, warmth or feeling in abundance
core_image: 石缝里一股细水不断涌出，在苔石上摊成一片亮面；灯罩向四周泼出暖黄的光；标本纸上一簇小花松散平展，枝条向四面摊开
scene: 山道旁的石缝里有一股细水不停涌出，在苔石上摊成一片发亮的水面。Clear water effuses from the crack and spreads over the mossy stone.
sceneCN: 这里 effuse 指「像液体那样流出、涌出」（第 1 个义项：流出；涌出）；句意是清水从石缝里涌出，摊过苔石。图中可辨识物件：石缝、细水流、苔石、发亮水面。

pos.zh: 流出；涌出；散发
（植物、贝壳）平展的；散开的

senses.title: To pour forth
senses.definition: to pour out or flow forth
senses.definitionCN: （动词）流出；涌出
senses.example: Clear water effuses from the crack and spreads over the mossy stone.
senses.exampleCN: 清水从石缝里涌出，摊过苔石。
senses.why: A thin stream welling out of a rock crack into a bright sheet on moss.
senses.whyCN: 一股细水从石缝里涌出，在苔石上摊成一片发亮的水面。

senses.title: To give off in abundance
senses.definition: to send out light, warmth or feeling freely and in large amounts
senses.definitionCN: （动词）大量地发出光、热或情感

dict_mnemonic.text: effuse ＝ ef-（向外，ex- 在 f 前的变体）＋ fuse（倾倒，拉丁 fundere／fusus）＝「向外倒」。记住 fus- 这一家按前缀分方向：ef-（外）→ effuse 流出、effusion 流出／积液、effusive 感情往外倒＝热情洋溢的；dif-（分开）→ diffuse 扩散；in-（向内）→ infuse 注入、泡茶；con-（一起）→ confuse 倒在一起＝混淆；pro-（向前）→ profuse 大量倾泻＝丰富的。日常英语里 effuse 作动词较少见，更常见的是 effusive（热情洋溢的）与 effusion（流出；积液）。植物学、贝壳学里 effuse 作形容词，指「松散平展的」。

dict_mnemonic.text: effusive ＝ ef-（向外）＋ fus（倾倒，拉丁 fundere）＋ -ive（形容词后缀，有…性质的）＝「往外倒的」。把感情往外倒 → 热情洋溢的、溢于言表的，常带一点「过头了」的意味：effusive praise 溢于言表的赞美、an effusive welcome 热情的欢迎。同一家族：effuse 动词「流出」、effusion 名词「流出；迸发；积液」、effusively 副词、effusiveness 名词。地质学里 effusive rock 指喷出岩（熔岩倒出地表冷凝），与 intrusive 侵入岩相对。近义 gushing 更口语、更贬；demonstrative 中性，指感情外露；profuse 只说数量大（profuse thanks 连声道谢），不评价是否过头。

dict_mnemonic.text: egoism ＝ ego（拉丁语「我」）＋ -ism（学说、主义）＝「以我为先的主义」。词尾换一换就换词性：-ist → egoist 利己主义者（人）；-istic → egoistic 利己主义的（形容词）；-istically → egoistically。哲学里分两支：ethical egoism 伦理利己主义（「人应当为自己」），psychological egoism 心理利己主义（「人本来就只为自己」）。关键辨析：egotism 多一个 t，那个 t 记作 talk，指「老说自己」＝自我吹嘘；egoism 指「只算自己」＝利己。反义词 altruism 利他主义（alter ＝ 他人）。日常说「自私」用 selfishness，egoism 偏理论与书面。

root: 拉丁语 ego（我）＋ -ism（学说）→ egoism（利己主义；自我中心）

senses.title: Planned in great detail
senses.definition: worked out with great care and in many steps, as a plan or system
senses.definitionCN: 经过细致推敲、步骤繁多，如计划或体系
senses.example: They worked out an elaborate plan for the escape.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为逃跑制定了一套周密的计划。
senses.why: A plan is also a thing made, so the same word covers the labour of thought rather than of hands.
senses.whyCN: 计划同样是被做出来的东西，于是同一个词也能覆盖头脑的劳作而不只是手上的。

senses.title: To explain more fully
senses.definition: to add more detail to what has been said or written
senses.definitionCN: 为已说或已写的内容补充更多细节
senses.example: Could you elaborate on that last point?
senses.exampleCN: 你能就最后一点详细说明吗？
senses.why: To elaborate is to keep working the material until the shape is complete, so speech is treated like wood.
senses.whyCN: elaborate 就是继续加工材料直到形状完整，于是言语也被当成木头来雕。

intro.en: Elaborate comes from Latin elaboratus, the past participle of elaborare, to labour out, from e- out plus laborare, to work.
intro.cn: elaborate 来自拉丁语 elaboratus，即 elaborare（费力做出）的过去分词，由 e-（出）加 laborare（劳作）构成。

items.en: Labor meant toil or effort, the noun behind the verb.
items.cn: labor 意为「辛劳、费力」，是动词背后的名词。

items.en: The verb meant to work, to toil or to be in difficulty.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「劳作、辛苦、处于困难」。

items.en: E- out plus laborare formed the verb to work out or take pains over.
items.cn: e-（出）加 laborare 构成「做出来、为之费力」的动词。

items.en: The participle described something worked out with care, hence finely made.
items.cn: 分词描述经过仔细加工而成的东西，因此是「精细制作的」。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective for ornamented things and later formed a verb from it.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词指装饰繁复之物，后来又由它造出动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elaboration family; the near-meaning group separates intricate, detailed and ornate.
note.cn: 形近组收 elaboration 词族；近义组区分 intricate、detailed 与 ornate。

entries.definition: The act of explaining in more detail, or of working something out fully.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「详述；精心制作」，由 elaborate 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: In a detailed or heavily ornamented manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「繁复地；精心地」。

entries.definition: Work, especially hard physical work; the root of elaborate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「劳动」，是本词的词根来源。

entries.definition: Having many small parts arranged in a way that is hard to follow.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「错综复杂的」，强调难以看清的结构。

entries.definition: Containing many facts or small points, without the sense of ornament.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「详细的」，只有细节多，不含装饰义。

entries.definition: Richly decorated; it stresses decoration rather than planning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「华丽装饰的」，强调装饰而非谋划。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a carving knife, then move to a plan on paper and finally to a speaker adding detail.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一把刻刀出发，再走到纸上的计划，最后落到补充细节的说话人。

normal.en: Elaborate carries labour in it: every extra part cost work.
normal.cn: elaborate 里藏着 labour：每多一个部件都是劳作。

normal.en: A carved table leg is elaborate; a plain one is not.
normal.cn: 雕花的桌腿是 elaborate，光的就不是。

normal.en: A plan can be as elaborate as a carving.
normal.cn: 一份计划可以和一件雕刻一样繁复。

normal.en: To elaborate on a point is to keep carving it.
normal.cn: elaborate on 一点，就是继续雕那一点。

normal.en: Elaborate is the adjective; elaborate is also the verb, same spelling.
normal.cn: elaborate 既是形容词也是动词，拼写相同。

abstract.en: Picture a woodcarver who refuses to leave a surface plain.
abstract.cn: 想象一位不肯让任何平面空着的木雕师。

abstract.en: The same patience can go into a table, a plan, or an answer.
abstract.cn: 同一份耐性可以用在桌子、计划或一个回答上。

abstract.en: Elaborate means the work has been worked again and again.
abstract.cn: elaborate 意味着这件东西被一遍遍加工过。

examples.en: The table has an elaborate carved base.
examples.cn: 这张桌子的底座雕工繁复。

examples.en: They worked out an elaborate plan for the escape.
examples.cn: 他们为逃跑制定了一套周密的计划。

examples.en: Could you elaborate on that last point?
examples.cn: 你能就最后一点详细说明吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊拉伯瑞特」——桌腿刻满缠枝纹，一刀也不肯省

root: 拉丁语 laborare「劳作」加前缀 e-「出」构成 elaborare「费力做出」，其过去分词 elaboratus 意为「精心做成的」，英语借入为形容词，后又用作动词「详述」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elaborate: richly made, carefully planned in detail, and the verb meaning to explain more fully.
sensesIntro.cn: elaborate 的三个义项：制作繁复、谋划周密，以及动词「详细阐述」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carved table leg covered in dense vine patterns, no cut spared.
core.cn: 核心意象：雕满细密缠枝纹的桌腿，一刀也不省。

branches.en: THE CARVING: many parts, each one worked by hand.
branches.cn: 雕工线：部件众多，每一件都手工加工。

branches.en: THE PLAN: the same patience spent on thought instead of wood.
branches.cn: 计划线：同一份耐性用在思虑而非木头上。

branches.en: THE EXPLANATION: the speaker keeps working the point.
branches.cn: 说明线：说话人继续加工那一点。

branches.en: THE DETAIL: whether hands or head, the detail is deliberate.
branches.cn: 细节线：无论用手还是用脑，细节都是有意加的。

branches.en: THE UNFOLDING: a detailed plan and a detailed answer both open outward.
branches.cn: 展开线：周密的计划与详尽的回答都向外铺开。

intro.en: Elaborate is e- plus the Latin labour verb; English then adds -ion, -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: elaborate 是 e- 加拉丁语「劳作」动词；英语随后再加 -ion、-ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor, laborare and elaboratus are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 labor、laborare 与 elaboratus 均有记录，只有更深的印欧词根属于重构。

items.example: It is the noun behind the verb.

items.exampleCN: 它与 laborare 构成 elaborare。

items.example: It is the direct source verb.
It is the source of the adjective.

definition_zh: 详述；精心制作；细化；附加细节；理论或计划的展开；装饰性加工；认知精细加工（心理学）；生物结构的复杂化
definition_en: the act or result of working something out in detail, adding parts or explanation until it is full; also, the added detail itself
core_image: 一张草图被一层层加上标注、剖面和箭头，最后密得几乎盖住原线
scene: 一张粗略的草图被标签、分区与箭头盖满，原来的线条几乎看不见了。A rough sketch is covered with labels, sections and arrows until the original line is almost hidden. Every added label and arrow is part of the elaboration of that sketch.
sceneCN: 这里 elaboration 是「逐层添加细节、把东西做细」（第 1 个义项：详述、细化）；句意：每一条标注与箭头都是那张草图细化的一部分。图中可辨识物件：草图、标注线、剖面图、箭头、叠放的描图纸。

pos.zh: 详述；细化；精心制作；附加细节

derivatives.zh: 详细阐述；精心制作；复杂精细的

senses.title: Working it out in detail: adding until it is full
senses.definition: the act of developing something in detail by adding parts, steps, or explanation
senses.definitionCN: 通过添加部分、步骤或说明来详细展开某事的行为
senses.example: The plan needed elaboration before anyone could build from it.
senses.exampleCN: 这份计划需要细化，别人才能照着施工。
senses.why: Elaboration is Latin elaboratio, from elaborare 'to labor out', ex- 'out' plus laborare 'to work'. The image is work applied until the thing comes out complete.
senses.whyCN: elaboration 是拉丁语 elaboratio，源于 elaborare“劳作而成”，即 ex-“出”加 laborare“工作”。意象是不断施力，直到东西完整地出来。

senses.title: The added detail itself: an amplification
senses.definition: a particular added explanation, example, or ornament that develops a point
senses.definitionCN: 用来展开某一要点的具体补充说明、例证或修饰
senses.example: His speech was full of elaborations that obscured the main claim.
senses.exampleCN: 他的演讲满是铺陈，反而遮住了主要论点。
senses.why: The action noun can shift to its product, as 'building' can mean a building. Here elaboration is a thing added, not the process of adding.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词可以转指其产物，正如 building 既可指建造也可指建筑物。这里的 elaboration 是被加上的东西，而不是添加的过程。

senses.title: Theory development: extending a model
senses.titleCN: 理论展开：把模型往外扩
senses.definition: the extension of a theory or model with further distinctions and mechanisms
senses.definitionCN: 用更多区分与机制来扩展某一理论或模型
senses.example: The paper's elaboration of the model added three testable predictions.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文对模型的展开增加了三项可检验的预测。
senses.why: In research, elaboration is not decoration but specification: each added part must be capable of being tested. The 'labor' is intellectual.
senses.whyCN: 在研究中，elaboration 不是装饰而是具体化：每个添加部分都必须可被检验。这里的“劳作”是智力上的。

senses.title: Plan detail: from outline to instructions
senses.titleCN: 计划细节：从提纲到作业指导
senses.definition: the conversion of a general plan into detailed, actionable steps
senses.definitionCN: 把总体计划转化为详细可执行的步骤
senses.example: The elaboration of the schedule took longer than the design.
senses.exampleCN: 把进度表细化所花的时间比设计还长。
senses.why: A plan is elaborated when every step has an owner and a time. The noun measures the distance between an intention and a set of instructions.
senses.whyCN: 当每一步都有责任人和时间，计划就被细化了。这个名词衡量“意图”与“一套指令”之间的距离。

senses.title: Spoken expansion: saying more about it
senses.titleCN: 口头铺陈：就这一点多说几句
senses.definition: the act of expanding on a point in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在口头或书面表达中对某一要点加以展开
senses.example: The chair asked for elaboration on the second recommendation.
senses.exampleCN: 主席要求就第二项建议作进一步说明。
senses.why: This is the metalinguistic sense: 'could you elaborate?' asks for more words, not more parts. The labor is now verbal.
senses.whyCN: 这是元语言层面的义项：“能不能 elaborate 一下？”要的是更多话，而不是更多零件。此时的“劳作”是言辞上的。

senses.title: Ornamental working: the detail that is craft
senses.titleCN: 装饰性加工：细节本身就是工艺
senses.definition: intricate workmanship or ornamentation added to an object or design
senses.definitionCN: 加在物件或设计上的繁复工艺或装饰
senses.example: The carving's elaboration marks it as a master's work.
senses.exampleCN: 这件雕刻的繁复细节表明它是大师之作。
senses.why: Here the added parts are not for clarity but for beauty. The same word covers both explanation and ornament because both require prolonged labour.
senses.whyCN: 这里加上的部分不是为了清楚，而是为了美。同一个词既覆盖说明也覆盖装饰，因为两者都需要长时间的劳作。

senses.title: Cognitive elaboration: linking new to known
senses.titleCN: 认知精细加工：把新的接到已知上
senses.definition: the mental process of connecting new information to existing knowledge to aid memory
senses.definitionCN: 把新信息与已有知识联系起来以帮助记忆的心理过程
senses.example: Elaboration improved recall more than repetition did.
senses.exampleCN: 精细加工比重复更能改善回忆。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word for depth of processing: the learner adds links, examples and inferences. The added parts are now mental connections.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借这个词指加工深度：学习者加上联系、例子与推论。此时被加上的部分是心理联结。

senses.title: Biological elaboration: structure growing complex
senses.titleCN: 生物复杂化：结构越长越复杂
senses.definition: the evolutionary development of more complex structures or behaviours
senses.definitionCN: 更复杂的结构或行为在演化中的发展
senses.example: The elaboration of the shell parallels the elaboration of the burrow.
senses.exampleCN: 壳的复杂化与洞穴的复杂化是同步的。
senses.why: Evolutionary biology uses the noun for added structure, often with a cost: complexity is elaborated only when it pays. The 'labor' is blind selection over generations.
senses.whyCN: 演化生物学用这个名词指增加的结构，且常带代价：只有划算时复杂结构才会被 elaborat。这里的“劳作”是跨越世代的盲目选择。

intro.en: Elaboration comes from Latin elaboratio, from elaborare 'to labor out, work out', itself ex- 'out' plus laborare 'to work', from labor 'toil'. English borrowed it in the 16th century. The 'detail' sense and the 'ornament' sense both descend from the same image of prolonged work.
intro.cn: elaboration 出自拉丁语 elaboratio，源于 elaborare“劳作而成、做出”，即 ex-“出”加 laborare“工作”，而 labor 意为“辛劳”。英语于 16 世纪借入。‘细节’义与‘装饰’义都来自同一个“长时间劳作”的意象。

items.en: Psychology adopts elaboration for deep processing, and biology uses it for the evolution of complex structures.
items.cn: 心理学采用 elaboration 指深度加工，生物学用它指复杂结构的演化。

items.en: English elaboration is recorded, borrowed from Latin elaboratio with the sense of working something out fully.
items.cn: 英语 elaboration 见于记载，借自拉丁语 elaboratio，意为把某事做到底、做完整。

items.en: elaboratio is the action noun of elaborare: ex- 'out' plus laborare 'to work'. The noun names both the effort and its finished result.
items.cn: elaboratio 是 elaborare 的动作名词：ex-“出”加 laborare“工作”。这个名词既指付出的努力，也指完成的结果。

items.en: labor 'toil, hardship' is generally connected with PIE *slab- 'to slip, be weak', though the semantic path is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: labor“辛劳、艰难”一般认为与原始印欧语 *slab-“滑、虚弱”相关，但这条语义路径是重构而非有直接文献佐证，*slab- 为重构形式。

items.en: laboratory also comes from laborare 'to work', but through medieval Latin laboratorium, a place for work. It is a true relative, not a look-alike.
items.cn: laboratory 同样出自 laborare“工作”，但经由中世纪拉丁语 laboratorium（工作之处）。它是真正的同族词，不是撞形词。

note.en: The first group separates two true relatives from one different-root neighbour; the second compares words that share only part of the meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分两个真正的同族词和一个不同词根的撞形词；第二组比较只共享部分含义的词。

entries.definition: a room for scientific work. It comes from medieval Latin laboratorium, 'a place for labour', from the same laborare as elaboration.
entries.definitionCN: 进行科学工作的房间。它出自中世纪拉丁语 laboratorium“劳作之处”，与 elaboration 同用 laborare。

entries.definition: to work with others. It is con- 'together' plus laborare, so the labour is shared rather than detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人一起工作。它是 con-“共同”加 laborare，因此“劳作”是共享的，而非细化的。

entries.definition: relating to the lips. It comes from labium 'lip', which is not labor 'toil'.
entries.definitionCN: 与嘴唇相关的。它出自 labium“唇”，不是 labor“辛劳”。

entries.definition: the act of expanding a statement or signal. It stresses making bigger, while elaboration stresses adding worked-out parts.
entries.definitionCN: 对陈述或信号的扩展。它强调“变大”，而 elaboration 强调“加上做细的部分”。

entries.definition: the improvement of something by small changes. It stresses precision and polish rather than the addition of parts.
entries.definitionCN: 通过细微改动来改进。它强调精确与打磨，而不是增加部分。

entries.definition: a small individual feature. It names the part, while elaboration names the act of adding parts.
entries.definitionCN: 小的个别特征。它命名部分本身，而 elaboration 命名添加部分的行为。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: elaboration is e- 'out' plus labor 'work' plus -ation: working something out until it is complete.
normal.cn: elaboration 是 e-“出”＋labor“劳动”＋-ation：一直把东西做出来、做到完整。

normal.en: The same labor gives laboratory, laborious and collaborate; all involve work, not lips.
normal.cn: 同一个 labor 给出 laboratory、laborious、collaborate，都关乎劳作，而非嘴唇。

normal.en: laboratory is a true relative: laboratorium means 'a place for work'.
normal.cn: laboratory 是真正的同族词：laboratorium 意为“工作之处”。

normal.en: labial comes from labium 'lip', which only looks like labor.
normal.cn: labial 出自 labium“唇”，只是看起来像 labor。

normal.en: Could you elaborate? means 'add words', while cognitive elaboration means 'add mental links'.
normal.cn: Could you elaborate? 意思是“多说几句”，而 cognitive elaboration 是“增加心理联结”。

abstract.en: Picture a sketch buried under labels, sections and arrows until the first line is almost gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一张草图被标注、剖面与箭头埋住，最初的线条几乎消失。

abstract.en: The same layers become a theory, a schedule, a speech, a carving, a memory and a shell.
abstract.cn: 同样的层层叠加可以变成理论、进度表、演讲、雕刻、记忆与贝壳。

abstract.en: Every sense asks how much worked-out material was added, and whether it helped or merely encrusted.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在问：加了多多少经加工的材料，以及它是帮了忙，还是只堆成了壳。

examples.en: The proposal is sound but needs elaboration before funding.
examples.cn: 这个提案是合理的，但在拨款前需要细化。

examples.en: Her elaboration of the theory connected three separate literatures.
examples.cn: 她对理论的展开把三支彼此分离的文献连了起来。

examples.en: Elaboration during study helps memory more than rereading.
examples.cn: 学习时的精细加工比反复阅读更有助于记忆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一拉玻璃拉深」——一层层拉、一层层加深，细节越做越细 → elaboration 详述、细化

root: 拉丁语 elaboratio“劳作而成”＝elaborare（ex-“出”＋laborare“工作”，源于 labor“辛劳”）＋-atio（动作名词后缀）。核心是“持续下功夫，直到细节完整地长出来”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: work added layer by layer until the thing is full. What changes is what the layers are — steps, explanations, ornaments, mental links, or evolved structures.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一层层加上功夫，直到东西变完整。变化的只是这些层是什么——步骤、说明、装饰、心理联结，或演化出的结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sketch buried under labels, sections and arrows until the first line nearly disappears.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张草图被标注、剖面与箭头层层埋住，最初的线条几乎不见。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PRODUCT: the labour of detailing and the detail that results share one noun.
branches.cn: 过程与产物：细化的劳作与由此产生的细节共用一个名词。

branches.en: SPECIFICATION: a theory or plan is elaborated until each added part can be tested or executed.
branches.cn: 具体化：理论或计划被展开，直到每个添加部分都可检验或可执行。

branches.en: WORDS: in conversation the added parts are sentences, and 'elaborate' means 'say more'.
branches.cn: 言辞：在对话中，被加上的部分是句子，elaborate 意为“多说一些”。

branches.en: CRAFT: when the added parts serve beauty rather than clarity, the same labour becomes ornament.
branches.cn: 工艺：当添加的部分服务于美而非清楚，同一种劳作就变成装饰。

branches.en: INNER AND EVOLVED LAYERS: the mind adds links to remember, and evolution adds structures that must pay for themselves.
branches.cn: 内在与演化的层：心智加上联结以记住，演化加上必须自偿其成本的结构。

intro.en: Elaboration is elaborate plus -ion. The suffix -ion, from Latin -ionem, names an action or its result; elaborate is Latin elaborare, ex- 'out' plus laborare 'to work'.
intro.cn: elaboration 是 elaborate 加 -ion。后缀 -ion 出自拉丁语 -ionem，表示动作或其结果；elaborate 是拉丁语 elaborare，即 ex-“出”加 laborare“工作”。

latinIntro.en: labor 'toil' supplies laborare 'to work'; the same family gives labor, laborious, laboratory and collaborate. labium 'lip' is a different root and accounts for labial.
latinIntro.cn: labor“辛劳”提供 laborare“工作”；同一词族给出 labor、laborious、laboratory、collaborate。labium“唇”是另一个词根，给出 labial。

items.meaning: the act or result of working something out in detail

intro.en: Elapse is Latin elapsus, slipped away, from elabi, which joins ex- meaning away to labi meaning to slip; the same laps- root gives lapse, collapse and relapse.
intro.cn: elapse 就是拉丁语 elapsus（已溜走的），来自 elabi，它把 ex-（离开）与 labi（滑动）结合；同一个 laps- 词根给出 lapse、collapse 与 relapse。

items.en: Latin labi means to slip or glide.
items.cn: 拉丁语 labi 意为滑动、溜走。

items.en: Adding ex- gives elabi, to slip away.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 elabi，意为溜走。

items.en: The participle elapsus means slipped away.
items.cn: 分词 elapsus 意为已溜走的。

items.en: English took elapse in the 15C, and only time could elapse.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪借用 elapse，而且只有时间能 elapse。

items.en: The noun lapse named a slipping away of time or of duty.
items.cn: 名词 lapse 指时间或职责的悄悄流失。

items.en: Science used elapsed time for the interval measured on a clock.
items.cn: 科学用 elapsed time 指时钟量出的时间间隔。

note.en: Elapse, lapse and collapse all carry laps-, the Latin root for slipped; elapse is only for time, lapse adds the idea of a small failure.
note.cn: elapse、lapse 与 collapse 都带着 laps-，那是拉丁语「滑动」的词根；elapse 只用于时间，lapse 还多了「小失误」的意思。

dict_mnemonic.text: elapse ＝ e-（离开，ex- 的变体）＋ lapse（滑动，拉丁 labi／lapsus）＝「滑走」。关键限制：elapse 的主语只能是时间（time, years, minutes, hours），不能说「人 elapse」。同根一家：lapse 名词「小失误；（时间）流逝」，动词「失效」（membership lapses 会员资格失效）；collapse ＝ col-（一起）＋ lapse ＝ 一起滑倒＝倒塌、崩溃；relapse ＝ re-（回）＋ lapse ＝ 滑回去＝复发；elapsed 形容词「已过去的」，elapsed time 已用时间。日常口语说 time passes / time goes by，elapse 偏书面与计时语境。近义 expire 指「到期」（护照、合同），intervene 指「（时间）介于其间」。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（离开）＋ labi（滑动）→ elabi → elapsus（已溜走的）→ elapse（时间消逝）

definition_zh: 有弹性的；可伸缩的；灵活的；橡皮筋
definition_en: able to stretch and return to its shape, able to change or be changed easily, or a rubber band
core_image: 一根橡皮筋被拉到两倍长，一松手又缩回原样
scene: 她把那根旧橡皮筋绕了两圈，纸卷始终没散。A thick elastic held the rolled papers together.
sceneCN: 这里 elastic 是「橡皮筋」（第 4 个义项：可拉伸回弹的环状橡胶制品）；句意是一根粗橡皮筋把卷好的纸捆住了。

senses.title: Able to stretch and spring back
senses.definition: able to be stretched and then return to its original shape
senses.definitionCN: 能够被拉伸，随后又恢复原来的形状
senses.example: The fabric is elastic enough to fit any wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 这块布料弹性足够，什么手腕都套得上。
senses.why: Elastic was coined from a Greek word for beaten metal that springs back, so the idea is a shape that returns.
senses.whyCN: elastic 由希腊语中表示「被敲打后能回弹的金属」的词造出，核心就是「会恢复的形状」。

senses.title: Able to change easily
senses.definition: able to change, adapt or be stretched in meaning without breaking
senses.definitionCN: 能够改变、适应，或在含义上被拉宽而不致崩坏
senses.example: The timetable is elastic enough to absorb delays.
senses.exampleCN: 这份时间表灵活得足以吸收延误。
senses.why: A material that springs back suggests a rule that gives and returns, so the adjective moves from rubber to arrangements.
senses.whyCN: 能回弹的材料让人想到一条会让步又收回的规则，于是这个形容词从橡皮走到了安排上。

senses.title: Responsive to price or demand
senses.definition: in economics, changing noticeably when price or income changes
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，随价格或收入变化而明显变化
senses.example: Demand for flights is highly elastic in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季的机票需求弹性很大。
senses.why: A quantity that stretches with price behaves like rubber, so economists borrowed the same image.
senses.whyCN: 随价格伸缩的数量表现得像橡皮，于是经济学家借用了同一个意象。

senses.title: A rubber band
senses.definition: a loop of stretchy rubber used to hold things together
senses.definitionCN: 用来把东西捆在一起的环状弹性橡胶
senses.example: A thick elastic held the rolled papers together.
senses.exampleCN: 一根粗橡皮筋把卷好的纸捆住了。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the thing made of the material, the way a name for a quality becomes an object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成了用这种材料做成之物的名词，就像一种性质的名称变成了实物。

intro.en: Elastic was coined in the seventeenth century from Greek elastos, beaten or ductile, and Latin elasticus, in the new science of materials.
intro.cn: elastic 是十七世纪在材料新科学中造出的词，源自希腊语 elastos（可敲打延展的）与拉丁语 elasticus。

items.en: The verb meant to drive or set in motion, and it lies behind the later adjective.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「驱动、推动」，是后来形容词的深层来源。

items.en: Elastos described metal that could be beaten out and would spring back.
items.cn: elastos 描述可被敲打成薄片又会回弹的金属。

items.en: Modern Latin formed elasticus as a technical adjective for materials.
items.cn: 近代拉丁语构成 elasticus，作为材料的专业形容词。

items.en: Seventeenth-century writers used elastic for gases and springs that recover their shape.
items.cn: 十七世纪的作者用 elastic 指能恢复形状的气体与弹簧。

items.en: The word spread to cloth, timetables, prices and finally to the rubber band itself.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到布料、时间表、价格，最后连橡皮筋本身也叫 elastic。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elasticity family; the near-meaning group separates flexible, springy and plastic.
note.cn: 形近组收 elasticity 词族；近义组区分 flexible、springy 与 plastic。

entries.definition: Bands or strips of stretchy material, used in the plural.

entries.definition: Able to bend without breaking; it stresses bending rather than springing back.

entries.definition: Bouncing back quickly, like a spring; more concrete and physical.

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one rubber band, then let the same springiness travel into plans and prices.

normal.en: Stretch it, let go, and it returns: that is elastic.
normal.cn: 拉长、松手、回到原样：这就是 elastic。

normal.en: An elastic timetable gives way and then closes again.
normal.cn: 有弹性的时间表会让步，然后又收回去。

normal.en: Economists call demand elastic when buyers stretch away from a price rise.
normal.cn: 价格上涨时买家就缩手，经济学家称这种需求为 elastic。

normal.en: The band itself takes the name: a bag of elastics.
normal.cn: 橡皮筋本身也用了这个名字：一袋 elastics。

normal.en: In- turns it stiff: inelastic.
normal.cn: 加 in- 就变硬：inelastic。

abstract.en: The same give-and-return can describe a rule, a price or a schedule.

definition_en: the ability of a material to return to its original shape after being stretched or compressed, or the responsiveness of a quantity to a change in another

scene: 橡皮筋被拉长到两倍，松手后立刻缩回原来的长度，没有留下永久变形。Rubber shows elasticity when it returns to its original length after being stretched.
sceneCN: 这里指材料被拉伸后恢复原状的能力（第 1 个义项：弹性）；句意为橡胶在拉伸后恢复原长，显示出弹性。图中可辨识物件：橡皮筋、拉伸的手指、标尺、原长虚线、回弹箭头。

pos.zh: 弹性；回弹性；伸缩性；灵活性

senses.title: Return to the original shape
senses.definition: the property of a material that lets it return to its original shape after a stretching or squeezing force is removed
senses.definitionCN: 材料在拉力或压力去除后恢复原有形状的性质
senses.example: The elasticity of the rubber seal keeps the joint tight.
senses.exampleCN: 橡胶密封件的弹性使接头保持紧密。
senses.why: The Greek source meant ductile or flexible, and physics narrowed it to the ability to spring back.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为可延展、柔韧，物理学把它收窄为弹回的能力。

senses.title: The response of demand
senses.definition: the degree to which the quantity demanded changes when price or income changes
senses.definitionCN: 价格或收入变化时，需求量随之变化的程度
senses.example: Elasticity of demand was high for the cheaper parts.
senses.exampleCN: 较便宜零件的需求弹性较高。
senses.why: Economists borrowed the material word because demand also stretches and shrinks in response to a pull.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家借用了材料词，因为需求也会随拉力伸缩。

senses.title: The response of supply
senses.definition: the degree to which the quantity supplied changes when price changes
senses.definitionCN: 价格变化时供给量随之变化的程度
senses.example: Low elasticity of supply kept prices rising.
senses.exampleCN: 供给弹性低使价格持续上升。
senses.why: Supply stretches less easily than demand in many markets, and the word carries that image.
senses.whyCN: 许多市场里供给比需求更难伸缩，这个词带着那个画面。

senses.title: The bounce of rubber
senses.definition: the strong, quick recovery of a rubbery material after large deformation
senses.definitionCN: 橡胶类材料在大形变后强烈而迅速地恢复
senses.example: Rubber elasticity comes from long molecules unfolding.
senses.exampleCN: 橡胶弹性来自长分子链的展开。
senses.why: Rubber stretches many times its length, and its return is the most visible example of the property.
senses.whyCN: 橡胶能拉到原长的许多倍，它的回缩是这种性质最直观的例子。

senses.title: Stretch in a physical sense
senses.definition: the ability of a body to extend and recover without breaking
senses.definitionCN: 物体能够伸长并恢复而不断裂的能力
senses.example: The elasticity of the fabric lets it fit any frame.
senses.exampleCN: 这种布料的伸缩性使其适合任何框架。
senses.why: Textiles and skin also stretch and return, and the word covers any such body.
senses.whyCN: 织物与皮肤同样会伸长再回缩，这个词覆盖任何这类物体。

senses.title: Flexibility in rules
senses.definition: the ability of a system, rule or schedule to change without breaking
senses.definitionCN: 制度、规则或安排能够改变而不崩溃的能力
senses.example: The elasticity of the schedule absorbed the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 进度安排的灵活性吸收了这次延误。
senses.why: A rule that can bend and recover is useful, and the physical metaphor made flexibility a virtue.
senses.whyCN: 能弯又能回的规则有用，物理比喻使「灵活」成为一种优点。

senses.title: A measured economic ratio
senses.titleCN: 经济学中量出的弹性系数
senses.definition: a numerical ratio expressing how much one economic variable responds to another
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个经济变量对另一个变量反应程度的数值比
senses.example: The study reported an elasticity of one point two.
senses.exampleCN: 研究报告给出的弹性系数为一点二。
senses.why: Once the metaphor became measurable, it turned into a ratio with a number attached.
senses.whyCN: 当比喻变得可测量，它就成了带数字的比值。

senses.title: Adaptability in a person
senses.definition: the ability of a person or arrangement to adapt to change and recover balance
senses.definitionCN: 人或安排适应变化并恢复平衡的能力
senses.example: Her elasticity under pressure impressed the crew.
senses.exampleCN: 她在压力下的变通能力让班组佩服。
senses.why: The same image of bending without breaking describes a temperament as well as a material.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「弯而不断」的画面，既能描述材料，也能描述性情。

intro.en: Elasticity comes from the adjective elastic, built in New Latin from Greek elastos, ductile or flexible, and the noun ending. The word was shaped in seventeenth-century physics and later spread to economics.
intro.cn: 这个词来自形容词 elastic，后者在新拉丁语中由希腊语 elastos「可延展、柔韧」加名词词尾构成。它在十七世纪物理学中成形，后来扩展到经济学。

items.en: Elastos meant ductile, beaten out or flexible, and it described metal that could be worked rather than broken.
items.cn: 这个词意为可延展的、被打薄的、柔韧的，描述可以加工而不折断的金属。

items.en: The related verb meant to drive, strike or beat out, and the connection to hammered metal is generally accepted.
items.cn: 相关动词意为驱动、击打、打薄，与锤打金属的联系一般认为成立。

items.en: Seventeenth-century science built the adjective elasticus from the Greek word, and English took it as elastic.
items.cn: 十七世纪科学由这个希腊词构成形容词 elasticus，英语以 elastic 借入。

items.en: Boyle and his contemporaries used elasticity for air and springs that return after compression; the first attestation date and the identity of the first user are both uncertain.
items.cn: 波义耳及其同时代人用这个词指受压后回弹的空气与弹簧；最早用例的首见年代与首见者都不确定。

items.en: Later physics separated elastic from plastic behaviour and made elasticity a measurable property.
items.cn: 后来的物理学把弹性行为与塑性行为分开，使弹性成为可测量的性质。

items.en: Nineteenth and twentieth-century economics applied the word to the response of prices, demand and supply.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪的经济学把这个词用于价格、需求与供给的反应。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like elasticity; the second group names neighbouring ideas of springing back and responsiveness.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「elasticity」相近；第二组是与「回弹、反应」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: Able to stretch and return, or a strip of such material.
entries.definitionCN: 指能拉伸回缩的，也指这种材料的带子。

entries.definition: In a way that springs back after deformation.
entries.definitionCN: 指以形变后回弹的方式。

entries.definition: Not returning to shape, or not responding much to price changes.
entries.definitionCN: 指不回弹的，或对价格变化反应不大的。

entries.definition: Made with stretchy material, usually of clothing.
entries.definitionCN: 指用弹性材料制成的，通常指衣物。

entries.definition: Oval in shape, or indirect in speech; it looks close but comes from a different Greek word.
entries.definitionCN: 指椭圆形的，或言语迂回的；形近但来自另一个希腊词。

entries.definition: The ability to recover quickly from compression, shock or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 指从压缩、冲击或困难中迅速恢复的能力。

entries.definition: The ability to bend without breaking, or to change plans easily.
entries.definitionCN: 指弯曲而不断裂的能力，或轻易改变计划的能力。

entries.definition: The quality of bouncing back after being pressed.
entries.definitionCN: 指受压后弹回的性质。

entries.definition: The degree to which something reacts to a change, used in economics and biology.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物对变化的反应程度，用于经济学与生物学。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Greek ductile source, the real physics family and real economics phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的希腊语「可延展」来源、真实物理同族词与真实经济学搭配。

normal.en: The Greek word described metal that could be beaten out, and the modern word describes a shape that comes back.
normal.cn: 希腊词描述能被锤薄的金属，现代词描述能回来的形状。

normal.en: Elastic and elasticity are the adjective and the noun of the same property.
normal.cn: elastic 与 elasticity 是同一性质的形容词与名词。

normal.en: Elasticity of demand and elasticity of supply are the two economics phrases.
normal.cn: 需求弹性与供给弹性是两个经济学说法。

normal.en: Inelastic means it will not stretch, in physics and in markets.
normal.cn: inelastic 意味着拉不动，物理与市场都通用。

normal.en: Rubber elasticity is the textbook example, because it can stretch several times its length.
normal.cn: 橡胶弹性是教科书例子，因为它能拉到原长的好几倍。

abstract.en: Elasticity is shape with a memory of where it came from.
abstract.cn: 弹性是有记忆的形状，记得自己原来在哪。

abstract.en: A market that stretches without breaking has elasticity too.
abstract.cn: 拉得开却不崩的市场也有弹性。

abstract.en: What bends and returns is trusted with more load next time.
abstract.cn: 弯了还能回来的东西，下次会被托付更多重量。

examples.en: The elasticity of the spring was tested at three temperatures.
examples.cn: 这根弹簧的弹性在三种温度下测试过。

examples.en: Price elasticity explains why the discount raised sales.
examples.cn: 价格弹性解释了为什么打折提升了销量。

examples.en: Old rubber loses its elasticity and starts to crack.
examples.cn: 老化的橡胶失去弹性并开始开裂。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL PROPERTY: rubber and fabric that extend and recover.

branches.cn: 橡胶回弹：长分子展开后把自己拉回去。

branches.cn: 市场反应：需求被价格拉动，供给被利润拉动，两者都量成比值。

branches.en: THE BENDING RULE: a schedule that gives and recovers without breaking.
branches.cn: 可弯的规则：能退让又能恢复、不会崩的安排。

branches.en: THE ADAPTABLE PERSON: someone who bends under pressure and comes back to balance.
branches.cn: 能变通的人：在压力下弯腰，再回到平衡。

intro.en: Elation is Latin elatio, a lifting up, from elatus, the participle of efferre, which joins ex- meaning out to ferre meaning to carry; the mood is carried upward.
intro.cn: elation 就是拉丁语 elatio（抬起），来自 elatus，它是 efferre 的分词，而 efferre 把 ex-（向外）与 ferre（携带）结合；情绪被向上抬了起来。

items.en: Latin ferre means to carry or bear.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ferre 意为携带、承受。

items.en: Adding ex- gives efferre, to carry out or lift up.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 efferre，意为带出、抬起。

items.en: The participle elatus means lifted up, carried out.
items.cn: 分词 elatus 意为被抬起的、被带出的。

items.en: The noun elatio names a lifting up, later a lifting of the spirits.
items.cn: 名词 elatio 指抬起，后来指情绪高涨。

items.en: English took elation in the 14C for pride and high spirits.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借用 elation，指自豪与高昂情绪。

items.en: Psychology used elation for an elevated mood that can overshoot judgement.
items.cn: 心理学用 elation 指可能超出判断力的高涨情绪。

dict_mnemonic.text: elation ＝ e-（向外、向上，ex- 的变体）＋ lat（携带，拉丁 ferre／latus）＋ -ion（名词后缀）＝「被抬起来的状态」。情绪被抬高 → 兴高采烈、得意洋洋。同根换词尾：elate 动词「使兴奋」、elated 形容词「兴高采烈的」（人作主语：she was elated）、elatedly 副词、elating 形容词「令人兴奋的」（事作主语）。注意与 elation 押韵的 relation 也来自 latus（relatus 带回），但意思完全不同。近义梯度：elation 成功后的喜悦自豪；euphoria 强度更高的欣快（也用于医学）；exhilaration 带刺激感的振奋（运动、速度）；jubilation 公开表达的欢腾。反义方向是 dejection（de- 向下 ＋ ject 扔 ＝ 情绪被扔下去＝沮丧）。

senses.title: The joint of the arm
senses.definition: the joint where the upper arm meets the forearm, and the bony point outside it

senses.example: He raised his elbow to shield the box.
senses.exampleCN: 他抬起肘护住箱子。
senses.why: Old English elnboga joined the word for forearm length with the word for bow, so the joint is literally an arm-bow.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 elnboga 把「前臂长度」与「弓」两个词拼在一起，这个关节字面就是「手臂之弓」。

senses.title: The part of a sleeve
senses.definition: the part of a garment that covers the elbow, often reinforced
senses.definitionCN: 衣服覆盖肘部的那一块，常做加固
senses.example: The jacket has leather patches on the elbows.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套的肘部有皮革补片。
senses.why: Clothing is named after the body part it covers, so the sleeve's bend is also an elbow.
senses.whyCN: 衣服的部件按它覆盖的身体部位命名，于是袖子的弯处也叫 elbow。

senses.title: To push with the elbow

intro.en: Elbow comes from Old English elnboga, a compound of eln, forearm, and boga, bow, the same bow of bow and arrow.
intro.cn: elbow 来自古英语 elnboga，由 eln（前臂）与 boga（弓）复合，boga 就是弓箭之「弓」。

items.en: The reconstructed noun named the forearm and also a unit of length.
items.cn: 重构名词既指前臂，也指一种长度单位。

items.en: Eln meant the forearm and the old measure called the ell.
items.cn: eln 指前臂，也指称为「厄尔」的旧长度单位。

items.en: Boga meant bow, the curved weapon and any arch.
items.cn: boga 意为「弓」，既是弯的武器，也指任何拱形。

items.en: The compound named the arm's bend, the elbow.
items.cn: 这个复合词指手臂弯处，即肘。

items.en: Middle English smoothed the middle of the word and settled elbowe.
items.cn: 中古英语磨平了词的中段，固定为 elbowe。

items.en: The verb use and the pipe sense grew from the shape and the joint.
items.cn: 动词用法与管道义分别从「形状」与「关节」长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds built on elbow; the near-meaning group separates joint, wrist, knee and shoulder.
note.cn: 形近组收由 elbow 构成的复合词；近义组区分关节与相邻部位。

entries.definition: Space to move freely, or freedom to act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「活动余地」，由 elbow 与 room 复合。

entries.definition: Having elbows, or shaped like a bent elbow.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有肘的；弯头状的」。

entries.definition: An old unit of length based on the forearm, from the same eln.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「厄尔」，以旧时前臂为准的长度单位，同出 eln。

entries.definition: Any place where two bones meet; the general word for what elbow names in particular.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「关节」，是 elbow 的上位词。

entries.definition: The joint between the forearm and the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腕」，是前臂与手之间的关节。

entries.definition: The corresponding joint in the leg, bent in the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「膝」，腿上以同样方式弯曲的对应关节。

entries.definition: The joint at the top of the arm, above the elbow.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「肩」，位于肘之上的关节。

normalIntro.en: These hooks take the arm as a bow, then follow the same bend into clothing, crowds and plumbing.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把手臂看成一张弓，再让同一个弯走进衣服、人群与管道。

normal.en: Elbow is an arm-bow: eln, forearm, plus boga, bow.
normal.cn: elbow 就是「手臂之弓」：eln（前臂）加 boga（弓）。

normal.en: Bend the arm and the sharp point sticks out.
normal.cn: 把手臂弯起来，那块尖骨就顶出来。

normal.en: A jacket's elbow is named after the joint inside it.
normal.cn: 外套的肘部按里面那个关节命名。

normal.en: To elbow through a crowd is to use that point as a tool.
normal.cn: 在人群里 elbow，就是拿那块尖骨当工具。

normal.en: A pipe elbow turns at the same angle as the arm.
normal.cn: 管道弯头拐出的角度和手臂一样。

abstract.en: Picture an arm bent into a right angle.
abstract.cn: 想象一条手臂弯成直角。

abstract.en: The same bend appears in a sleeve, in a queue, and in a water pipe.
abstract.cn: 同一个弯出现在袖子上、队伍里和一根水管里。

abstract.en: Elbow is a place where a straight line is forced to turn.
abstract.cn: elbow 就是一条直线被迫转弯的地方。

examples.en: He raised his elbow to shield the box.
examples.cn: 他抬起肘护住箱子。

examples.en: She elbowed her way to the front of the queue.
examples.cn: 她用肘挤到了队伍前面。

examples.en: A blocked elbow stopped the water flow.
examples.cn: 一个堵塞的弯头阻断了水流。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埃爾波」——手臂弯成直角，外侧顶出一块尖骨

root: 古英语 elnboga 由 eln「前臂」与 boga「弓」复合，字面即「手臂之弓」；eln 同时是旧长度单位「厄尔」的来源。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of elbow: the arm joint, the sleeve part covering it, the act of pushing with it, and a pipe's bend.
sensesIntro.cn: elbow 的四个义项：肘关节、衣服的肘部、用肘推挤，以及管道弯头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arm bent into a right angle with a sharp bone at the turn.
core.cn: 核心意象：手臂弯成直角，拐角处顶出一块尖骨。

branches.en: THE JOINT: the place where the arm folds.
branches.cn: 关节线：手臂折起来的地方。

branches.en: THE CLOTH: the sleeve section named after that joint.
branches.cn: 布料线：按那个关节命名的袖子部分。

branches.en: THE SHOVE: the hard point turned into a tool.
branches.cn: 推挤线：那块硬骨变成工具。

branches.en: THE PIPE: a metal arm bent at the same angle.
branches.cn: 管道线：一条以同样角度弯起的水管。

branches.en: ONE SHAPE: body and pipe share the same right-angle turn.
branches.cn: 同一形状：身体与管道共用同一个直角转弯。

intro.en: Elbow is a native Germanic compound of two old words; modern English adds -s, -ed and -ing.
intro.cn: elbow 是由两个古词构成的日耳曼语本土复合词；现代英语再加 -s、-ed 与 -ing。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin layer; both elements are Germanic and recorded in Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语层次；两个构件都属于日耳曼语，在古英语中均有记录。

items.example: It is the direct source form.
It descends from the same eln.

definition_zh: 年长的；上了年纪的；老年人
definition_en: rather old, used politely of people past middle age, or the group of old people as a whole
core_image: 公园长椅上，一位老人把围巾又拢紧了些
scene: 长椅上那位老人扶着扶手才站起来，动作很慢。An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
sceneCN: 这里 elderly 是「年长的」（第 1 个义项：客气地指已过中年、年纪较大的人）；句意是一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。

pos.zh: 年长的；上了年纪的（较礼貌）
老年人（集合用法）

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

senses.title: Rather old, said politely
senses.definition: past middle age and getting old, used as a polite word instead of old
senses.definitionCN: 已过中年、渐渐年老，用作 old 的客气说法
senses.example: An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
senses.exampleCN: 一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。
senses.why: Elderly is elder plus -ly, and elder is the comparative of old: it says older, gently, without the bluntness of old.
senses.whyCN: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly，而 elder 是 old 的比较级：它温和地说「更年长」，没有 old 那么直白。

senses.title: Old people as a group
senses.definition: with the, old people considered as a group in society
senses.definitionCN: 与 the 连用，指社会中作为一个群体的老年人
senses.example: The clinic offers free transport for the elderly.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为老年人提供免费接送。
senses.why: An adjective with the can name a whole class, so the elderly means all who answer to that description.
senses.whyCN: 形容词加 the 可以指整个类别，所以 the elderly 就是所有符合这个描述的人。

senses.title: Old and worn, said with a smile
senses.definition: used humorously of things that are old and worn out
senses.definitionCN: 戏谑地用于年久失修、老旧的物件
senses.example: My elderly laptop takes ten minutes to start.
senses.exampleCN: 我那台老掉牙的笔记本要十分钟才启动。
senses.why: The polite word for old people is transferred to machines, and the politeness itself becomes the joke.
senses.whyCN: 这个对人客气的词被挪到机器上，那份客气本身就成了笑话。

intro.en: Elderly is elder plus -ly; elder is the old comparative of old, from Old English eldra, and still carries the sense of seniority.
intro.cn: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly；elder 是 old 的古老比较级，来自古英语 eldra，至今仍带「辈分较长」的意味。

items.en: The reconstructed adjective meant old or grown up.
items.cn: 重构形容词意为「年老的、长成的」。

items.en: Eldra was the comparative of eald, old, and meant older.
items.cn: eldra 是 eald（老）的比较级，意为「更年长的」。

items.en: Elder kept the sense of senior in age or rank, especially within a family.
items.cn: elder 保留年龄或辈分较长的意思，尤用于家族内部。

items.en: The ending -ly softened the adjective into a polite description of age.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把这个形容词软化，成为对年龄的客气描述。

items.en: The elderly settled as a collective name, and the word spread jokingly to worn objects.
items.cn: the elderly 固定为集合称谓，这个词又戏谑地扩展到破旧物件上。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elder family; the near-meaning group separates old, senior and aged by tone.
note.cn: 形近组收 elder 词族；近义组按语气区分 old、senior 与 aged。

entries.definition: Older, especially of a relative or a person of authority in a community.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼名词，义为「年长的；长辈」，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The oldest of a group, usually of brothers or sisters.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最年长的」，多指兄弟姐妹中的老大。

entries.definition: Having lived a long time; plainer and blunter than elderly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「老的」，比 elderly 更直白。

entries.definition: Older or higher in rank, often used in official contexts such as senior citizens.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年长的、资深的」，常用于 senior citizens 等正式说法。

entries.definition: Very old; it can sound more formal or more pointed than elderly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「年迈的」，比 elderly 更正式或更强调。

entries.definition: Growing old, said of a process rather than a person's state.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「老龄化的」，描述过程而非人的状态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from elder as the gentle comparative of old, then follow the word into a group name and a joke about machines.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从 elder 这个温和的比较级出发，再走到群体称谓与关于机器的玩笑。

normal.en: Elderly is elder plus -ly: the polite way of saying older.
normal.cn: elderly 是 elder 加 -ly：说「更年长」时的客气说法。

normal.en: Old can sting; elderly steps back and leaves room.
normal.cn: old 可能刺人；elderly 往后退半步，留出余地。

normal.en: The elderly are not one person but a whole group.
normal.cn: the elderly 不是一个人，而是一整群人。

normal.en: My elderly laptop is a joke: the politeness is the point.
normal.cn: my elderly laptop 是个玩笑：那份客气本身就是笑点。

normal.en: Elderly usually starts around retirement age, old goes further.
normal.cn: elderly 大约从退休年龄起算，old 还要再往后。

abstract.en: Picture a slow rise from a park bench, hands on the armrest.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人双手扶着扶手，从公园长椅上慢慢起身。

abstract.en: The same politeness can cover a person, a group, or a tired machine.
abstract.cn: 同一份客气可以覆盖一个人、一群人，或一台疲惫的机器。

abstract.en: Elderly is old with a hand held out.
abstract.cn: elderly 就是伸出手扶一把的 old。

examples.en: An elderly man rose slowly from the bench.
examples.cn: 一位年长的男士慢慢从长椅上站起来。

examples.en: The clinic offers free transport for the elderly.
examples.cn: 这家诊所为老年人提供免费接送。

examples.en: My elderly laptop takes ten minutes to start.
examples.cn: 我那台老掉牙的笔记本要十分钟才启动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埃尔德利」——老人扶着扶手，才慢慢站起来

root: elderly 由 elder 加 -ly 构成；elder 是 old 的古老比较级（古英语 eldra），故本词字面即「更年长的」，语气比 old 委婉。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of elderly: politely old, old people as a group, and humorously worn out.
sensesIntro.cn: elderly 的三个义项：客气地说年长、作为群体的老年人，以及戏称物件老旧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old person rising slowly from a bench, one hand on the armrest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位老人扶着扶手，从长椅上慢慢起身。

branches.en: THE PERSON: past middle age, described politely.
branches.cn: 人物线：已过中年，用客气的方式描述。

branches.en: THE CLASS: with the, all such people together.
branches.cn: 群体线：加 the 指所有这样的人。

branches.en: THE JOKE: the same politeness spent on a tired laptop.
branches.cn: 玩笑线：同一份客气用在一台疲惫的笔记本上。

branches.en: THE TONE: the word's gentleness is what joins person and group.
branches.cn: 语气线：这个词的温和把个人与群体连在一起。

branches.en: THE TRANSFER: respect for age becomes mock respect for age in objects.
branches.cn: 转移线：对年岁的敬重变成对物件年岁的假敬重。

intro.en: Elderly is a native English adjective built on the old comparative elder with the ending -ly.
intro.cn: elderly 是英语本土形容词，由古老比较级 elder 加词尾 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are Germanic and recorded in Old English, so no Latin entry is claimed here.
latinIntro.cn: 两个构件都属于日耳曼语且在古英语中有记录，因此这里不列拉丁语条目。

items.example: It is the positive form behind elder.
items.exampleCN: 它是 elder 背后的原级。

items.example: It is the source of elder.
It is the base of elderly.

definition_zh: 选举；当选；选择（正式）
definition_en: the process of choosing someone by voting, the fact of being chosen, or a formal act of choosing
core_image: 投票站门口贴着一张名单，纸角被风吹起
scene: 晚上十点投票站关门，计票机随即开始运转。The election result came before midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 election 是「选举」（第 1 个义项：通过投票选出人的整个过程）；句意是选举结果在午夜前出来了。

pos.zh: 选举；当选；（正式）选择

senses.title: The process of voting someone in
senses.definition: the organized process in which people vote to choose someone for an office
senses.definitionCN: 人们投票为某个职位选出人选的整套组织过程
senses.example: The election result came before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 选举结果在午夜前出来了。
senses.why: Election is the noun of eligere, to pick out: the whole machinery exists for one act of picking.
senses.whyCN: election 是 eligere（挑出）的名词：整套机器只为一次「挑出」而存在。

senses.title: The fact of being chosen
senses.definition: the state or event of being chosen for a post, seen from the winner's side
senses.definitionCN: 从当选者角度看，被选上某个职位这一事实
senses.example: Her election to the board surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 她当选董事，没人感到意外。
senses.why: The same picking seen from inside the winner becomes a personal event rather than a public process.
senses.whyCN: 同一次挑选若从当选者内部看，就成了个人事件，而不是公共过程。

senses.title: A formal act of choosing
senses.definition: a deliberate choice between options, used in formal or religious language
senses.definitionCN: 在选项之间作出的慎重选择，用于正式或宗教语境
senses.example: He made a deliberate election to stay silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他有意选择了保持沉默。
senses.why: Before it meant voting, the word simply named a choice; that older sense survives in formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「投票」之前，这个词只指一次选择；这个更古老的意思仍活在正式文章里。

intro.en: Election comes from Latin electio, the noun of eligere, to pick out, formed from e- out and legere, to choose.
intro.cn: election 来自拉丁语 electio，即 eligere（挑出）的名词，由 e-（出）与 legere（挑选）构成。

items.en: Legere meant to gather or pick, and it also gave lecture and legend.
items.cn: legere 意为「收集、挑选」，也生出 lecture 与 legend。

items.en: E- out plus legere formed the verb to pick out from among others.
items.cn: e-（出）加 legere 构成「从众人中挑出」的动词。

items.en: Electio named the act of picking out, at first any choice at all.
items.cn: electio 指「挑出」的动作，最初泛指任何选择。

items.en: French narrowed the noun toward choosing a person for an office.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词窄化为「为职位选人」。

items.en: English used it for both the choice and the gathering that makes it.
items.cn: 英语既用它指选择本身，也指做出选择的那场集会。

items.en: The voting sense dominates, while the plain sense of choice survives in formal style.
items.cn: 投票义占了主导，而朴素的「选择」义仍留在正式文体中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elect family; the near-meaning group separates vote, ballot and referendum.
note.cn: 形近组收 elect 词族；近义组区分 vote、ballot 与 referendum。

entries.definition: To choose someone for an office by voting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「选举」，是本词的动词词基。

entries.definition: Filled by election, or a course freely chosen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词兼名词，义为「选举产生的；选修的；选修课」。

entries.definition: All the people entitled to vote in an election.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「全体选民」。

entries.definition: To work actively for a candidate or party in a campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「进行竞选活动」。

entries.definition: A single formal expression of choice, or the total recorded.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「投票、票数」，是选举里的单个动作或总票数。

entries.definition: The paper or system used to cast a vote, or the voting itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选票、无记名投票」，指投票用的纸或方式。

entries.definition: A direct vote by the public on a single question, not on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「公投」，就一个问题而非人选直接投票。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start at a polling station door, then look at the same event from the winner's side and from the older sense of choosing.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从投票站门口出发，再从当选者一侧与更古老的「选择」义回看同一件事。

normal.en: Election is eligere turned into a noun: one act of picking out.
normal.cn: election 就是 eligere 变成名词：一次「挑出」。

normal.en: A general election fills many seats on one day.
normal.cn: general election 在一天里填满许多席位。

normal.en: From the winner's chair, the election is a personal event.
normal.cn: 坐在当选者的椅子上，election 是一件私人的事。

normal.en: In formal prose, an election can be any deliberate choice.
normal.cn: 在正式文章里，an election 可以指任何慎重的选择。

normal.en: The whole family keeps the same root: elect, election, elector, electoral.
normal.cn: 整族词共用一个词根：elect、election、elector、electoral。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of names pinned beside a door.
abstract.cn: 想象门边钉着一张写满名字的纸。

abstract.en: The same sheet is a public process, a private triumph, or a quiet decision.
abstract.cn: 同一张纸既是公共过程、私人胜利，也可以是一次安静的决定。

abstract.en: Election is a crowd doing the work of one hand.
abstract.cn: election 是一群人在做一只手所做的事。

examples.en: The election result came before midnight.
examples.cn: 选举结果在午夜前出来了。

examples.en: Her election to the board surprised no one.
examples.cn: 她当选董事，没人感到意外。

examples.en: He made a deliberate election to stay silent.
examples.cn: 他有意选择了保持沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊莱克申」——投票站关门，名单上的名字被挑出来

root: 拉丁语 legere「挑选」加前缀 e-「出」构成 eligere「挑出」，其名词 electio 即「挑选」，经法语进入英语，词义收窄为「选举」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of election: the voting process, the fact of being chosen, and any formal choice.
sensesIntro.cn: election 的三个义项：投票过程、当选这一事实，以及正式场合的「选择」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a list of names pinned beside a polling station door.
core.cn: 核心意象：投票站门边钉着一张写满名字的纸。

branches.en: THE MACHINERY: the whole voting process with its rules.
branches.cn: 机器线：带规则的一整套投票过程。

branches.en: THE WIN: the same event seen from the chosen side.
branches.cn: 当选线：从被选中者一侧看同一件事。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: any deliberate choice, in formal prose.
branches.cn: 古义线：正式文章里任何慎重的选择。

branches.en: TWO SIDES: process and outcome are one act named twice.
branches.cn: 两面线：过程与结果，是同一个动作的两种叫法。

branches.en: THE ROOT: voting and choosing are the same picking out.
branches.cn: 词根线：投票与选择本是同一种「挑出」。

intro.en: Election is the Latin -io noun of elect; English adds -or, -al, -ate and -eer to build the family.

senses.title: Filled by election
senses.definition: of a post or body, filled or decided by voting rather than by appointment
senses.definitionCN: 指职位或机构，由投票产生而非任命
senses.example: The mayor holds an elective office.
senses.exampleCN: 市长这一职位是民选的。
senses.why: Elective is elect plus -ive: the post has the property of being filled by a picking out.
senses.whyCN: elective 是 elect 加 -ive：这个职位带有「靠挑出来填补」的性质。

senses.title: Chosen rather than required
senses.definition: of a course or subject, taken by choice and not required
senses.definitionCN: 指课程或科目，出于自愿而非必修
senses.example: Music is an elective subject at this school.
senses.exampleCN: 在这所学校，音乐是选修科目。
senses.why: A student picking a course repeats the same picking out, so the word moves from offices to classrooms.
senses.whyCN: 学生挑一门课重复的是同一种「挑出」，于是这个词从职位走到了教室。

senses.title: Having the right to vote
senses.definition: of a person or body, possessing the right to vote in elections
senses.definitionCN: 指人或机构，拥有在选举中投票的权利
senses.example: The upper house is partly elective and partly appointed.
senses.exampleCN: 上议院部分由选举产生，部分由任命产生。
senses.why: The right to do the picking is itself described by the same adjective, so elective also means entitled to vote.
senses.whyCN: 做这次「挑出」的权利也用同一个形容词描述，所以 elective 也指「有选举权」。

senses.title: A course freely chosen
senses.definition: a course that a student chooses to take rather than one required by the programme
senses.definitionCN: 学生自愿选择而非培养方案规定的课程
senses.example: Students may take one elective in their final year.
senses.exampleCN: 学生在最后一年可以修一门选修课。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the thing chosen, the way a quality becomes an object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成「被选中之物」的名词，就像一种性质变成了实物。

senses.title: Scheduled rather than urgent
senses.definition: of medical treatment, planned in advance rather than needed at once
senses.definitionCN: 指医疗处置，事先安排而非当下必须进行
senses.example: The operation was elective, so it could wait a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这台手术是择期的，所以可以等一个月。
senses.why: What can be chosen in time is what is not forced by emergency, so elective also marks the optional in medicine.
senses.whyCN: 能在时间上挑选的，就是不被急症逼迫的，所以 elective 在医学里也标出「可选择」的部分。

intro.en: Elective is Latin electivus, from eligere, to pick out, with the adjective ending -ivus; English uses it for posts, courses and treatments.
intro.cn: elective 是拉丁语 electivus，由 eligere（挑出）加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成；英语把它用于职位、课程与医疗。

items.en: Legere meant to pick or gather, the base of the family.
items.cn: legere 意为「挑选、收集」，是整个词族的词基。

items.en: E- out plus legere formed the verb to pick out.
items.cn: e-（出）加 legere 构成「挑出」的动词。

items.en: The adjective described something that operates by choice or election.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述靠选择或选举来运作的事物。

items.en: Church and university Latin applied it to offices that were filled by voting.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语把它用于靠投票填补的职位。

items.en: English added the school sense of a chosen course and the medical sense of planned treatment.
items.cn: 英语又加入「自选课程」与「择期治疗」两个义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elect family; the near-meaning group separates optional, voluntary and selective.
note.cn: 形近组收 elect 词族；近义组区分 optional、voluntary 与 selective。

entries.definition: To choose a person for a post by voting.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「选举」，是本词的词基。

entries.definition: The process of choosing by vote.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选举」。

entries.definition: A person with the right to vote.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「选民」。

entries.definition: Not required; it can be left out entirely, which elective courses cannot.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可选的」，可以完全不做，而选修课仍需修满学分。

entries.definition: Done by free will, often without pay or pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自愿的」，强调出于自由意志。

entries.definition: Careful about what is chosen, or affecting only some; from the same root but a different idea.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有选择的、严格挑选的」，同根而义不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a blank slot on a timetable, then widen to an elected post and a planned operation.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从课表上的一个空格出发，再扩到民选职位与择期手术。

normal.en: Elective is elect plus -ive: something filled or taken by choosing.
normal.cn: elective 是 elect 加 -ive：靠挑选来填补或取得的东西。

normal.en: An elective office is one you have to be voted into.
normal.cn: elective office 是必须靠投票才能坐上的职位。

normal.en: An elective course is a blank on the timetable you fill yourself.
normal.cn: elective course 是课表上由你自己填的空格。

normal.en: The noun elective means the course, not the choosing.
normal.cn: 名词 elective 指那门课，而不是选择这个动作。

normal.en: Elective surgery can wait; emergency surgery cannot.
normal.cn: 择期手术可以等，急诊手术不能等。

abstract.en: Picture a form with one line left empty on purpose.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，有一行被故意留空。

abstract.en: The same empty line can be a seat to be voted on, a course, or a date for surgery.
abstract.cn: 同一个空格可以是要投票的席位、一门课，或一个手术日期。

abstract.en: Elective marks whatever is left open to choice.
abstract.cn: elective 标记的是一切仍向选择敞开的东西。

root: 拉丁语 eligere「挑出」加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成 electivus，义为「靠选择或选举运作的」；英语据此发展出民选、选修、择期诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of elective: filled by vote, chosen rather than required, entitled to vote, a chosen course, and planned rather than urgent.
sensesIntro.cn: elective 的五个义项：民选的、选修的、有选举权的、选修课，以及择期而非紧急的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blank line on a timetable that a student fills in.
core.cn: 核心意象：课表上一条由学生自己填的空行。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: a seat that only votes can fill.
branches.cn: 职位线：只有投票才能填上的席位。

branches.en: THE SUBJECT: a course taken by preference.
branches.cn: 科目线：凭偏好选上的科目。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: the power to take part in the picking.
branches.cn: 权利线：参与这次挑选的权力。

branches.en: THE COURSE: the adjective becomes the thing chosen.
branches.cn: 课程线：形容词变成被选中之物。

branches.en: THE OPTIONAL: study and treatment both moved to a date of your choosing.
branches.cn: 可选线：学业与治疗都被挪到你挑选的时间。

intro.en: Elective is the Latin -ivus adjective of eligere; English adds -ly and keeps the same stem for elect and election.
intro.cn: elective 是 eligere 的拉丁语 -ivus 形容词；英语再加 -ly，并与 elect、election 共用同一词干。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 electivus 有记录，其词基动词也有书证，只有最古老的词根属于重构。
